- **Parent-Hub is on a branch called `Crew-app`, not main.** Its new files will land on that branch.
- **Vercel won't be affected.** Entire warned that Veteran and W-Crew-app deploy on Vercel. It saves its checkpoints as hidden git refs rather than branches, so pushing them shouldn't start Vercel builds.
- **Older sessions can be imported.** It found past Claude Code sessions in stl-zoning, Veteran and W-Crew-app that you can bring in with `entire import claude-code` in each repo. I haven't run that. Want me to?

The sign-up notification email is still open: tell me which address should get a notice when someone signs up.

lastPrompt: What is the best way to get the most recent satilate data?

content.text:
It depends on how much detail you need. The most recent images are blurry, and sharp images are usually weeks to years old.

| What you need | Best source | How fresh | Detail | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Has the site been cleared or graded? | **Sentinel-2**, in Copernicus Browser (browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu) | Every 2–5 days, when it isn't cloudy | 10 m: you see a field turn to dirt, not individual houses | Free |
| Same, every day | **Planet** (PlanetScope) | Daily | 3 m | Paid subscription |
| Count lots, see roads and foundations | **Nearmap** (photos from airplanes, not satellites) | Several flights a year over metros like Columbus and St. Louis | About 3 inches | Subscription, roughly a few thousand dollars a year |
| One sharp image of a specific site | **Vantor (formerly Maxar) or Airbus**, ordered through SkyWatch, UP42 or Apollo Mapping | Their archive, or a new photo taken on request | About 1 foot | Pay per order, usually with a minimum area |
| Good enough and free | **NAIP** (USDA), county aerial photos, Google Earth Pro, Esri Wayback | Every 1–2 years | 2 feet down to 3 inches | Free |

**What I'd do:**
- **To check a site this week:** use Copernicus Browser. It's free, takes about two minutes, and shows imagery from the last few days. It tells you whether clearing has started, not much more.
- **For regular, detailed looks at land deals:** Nearmap is the industry standard for builders and land teams. Its photos are aerial, far sharper than any satellite, and recent enough for site work.
- **For one sharp, recent image of a single site:** order one from SkyWatch or UP42.

**In the tracker:** the parcel lookup map could show Sentinel-2 imagery with a "last seen" date. It could even flag when a site near one of your watched areas turns from green to bare dirt, which usually means grading has started. That's free to build on Sentinel Hub's free tier. Nearmap could be added too if you get a subscription.

Is this for checking your own sites, watching what competitors are clearing, or something else? The answer changes which source is worth paying for.

Satellite images are live as an opt-in feature. To turn them on, open **New features** in the header and switch on **Satellite images of sites**.

**What you get:** a "Satellite" section on Parcel lookup results, and on project pages for projects that have a street address. It shows three images about a mile across, with a pin on the site:
- the latest clear pass (for the Fenton parcel I tested, Oct 21, five days ago)
- one from about 3 months earlier
- one from about a year earlier

Each image shows a **% green** figure: how much of the ground within about 250 m of the site is vegetation. A big drop usually means clearing or grading. Fields also go brown after harvest, which is why the year-earlier image is there to compare against.

**How it works:**
- It's free and needs no account or key. The images come from the European Space Agency's Sentinel-2 satellites through Microsoft's free imagery service.
- Each image is at 10 m per pixel: good for seeing whether ground has been cleared or graded, not for counting houses.
- Cloudy passes are skipped automatically. My first version let hazy passes, and passes from the edge of a satellite tile (partly black), through; I tightened the check and the retest came out clean.
- The first look at a new site takes about 5–7 seconds while it finds clear passes, and the result is reused for 6 hours.
- An "Explore every date" link opens the site in the European Space Agency's free viewer, where you can scroll through every pass.

**Worth knowing:**
- Only 2 of Lombardo's 8 projects have a street address, so the project pages will mostly show nothing until addresses are added. Parcel lookup works for any address in St. Charles or St. Louis County.
- If 10 m turns out to be too coarse, the imagery source can be swapped for a paid one like Nearmap or Planet without changing the pages.

A possible next step: alert you when a watched site loses a lot of green compared with a year earlier, which would flag new grading near your sites automatically.

Entire captured this session. GitHub rejected its first upload attempt but accepted the retry, so the checkpoint is now on GitHub.

input.content:
-- OYL (On Your Lot) lots: Chad's "OYL Tracker" spreadsheet moved into the site (/oyl). One row per lot, each tied to a
-- project (stage 'oyl', or 'closed' once the customer has bought the lot), so the lot also gets a map point, nearby
-- cases and satellite images. Diligence end and Lombardo's purchase date live on the project (diligence_expires_on,
-- closing_on), as on dashboard cards. Chad's data was loaded with SQL, not here, to keep prices out of the repo.
create table if not exists public.oyl_lots (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  project_id bigint not null unique references public.projects(id) on delete cascade,
  lot_type text check (lot_type in ('Walkout', 'In-Grade', 'Lookout', 'TBD')),
  ownership text check (ownership in ('Pending', 'Lombardo', 'Customer', 'In Diligence')),
  sales_status text check (sales_status in ('Reserved', 'Flashed', 'Customer Purchased')),
  flashed_on date,
  customer_purchased_on date,
  acquisition_price numeric,
  municipality_cost numeric,
  arb_cost numeric,
  site_cost numeric,          -- "Site Cost Doug/Travis"
  civil_engineer text,
  contract_price numeric,     -- the home contract (the sheet's "Flash Price" on closed lots)
  jpp_projection numeric,
  final_sale_price numeric,
  sign_status text,
  hoa_contact text,
  hoa_phone text,
  largest_home text,
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.oyl_lots enable row level security;
-- Same as projects for now: the site has no logins yet. Tighten with the rest when sign-in ships.
create policy "team_all_oyl_lots" on public.oyl_lots for all to authenticated using (true) with check (true);
create policy "public_all_oyl_lots" on public.oyl_lots for all to anon using (true) with check (true);

Chad's OYL tracker is now a page on the live site, loaded with his Oct 19 data, prices included. To see it, open **New features** and switch on **OYL lots page**; an **OYL lots** link then appears in the menu next to Projects.

**What's on the page:**
- **Working lots:** a table with every column from his sheet. That covers the dates, ownership, sales status, days to flash and days to customer purchase. It also has every price and cost (acquisition, municipality, ARB, site cost, total, contract price), plus civil engineer, sign status, HOA contact and phone. Each row has an Edit link, and "+ Add a lot" adds new ones with the same dropdowns as his sheet.
- **Lot-count box:** the dollar figures match his sheet. Lombardo owns 6 lots ($2,044,900). 2 of those have a customer who has flashed or reserved ($965,000), so 4 have no buyer yet ($1,079,900). 3 lots are under contract to purchase ($1,262,000).
- **Closed:** 804 Joyce Ann and 521 Kehr's Mill, with an added average: 51 days to flash and 107 days to customer purchase.

**Each lot is also a project.** All 12 addresses matched exactly in the Census address database, so every lot is on the map with nearby-case alerts and satellite images. The 10 active lots show in the OYL column on the dashboard. Each lot's project page links to its lot details and prices. Changing a lot's ownership to Customer moves it to Closed. Ballwin is now followed so its meetings get collected, since five of the lots are there.

**Check with Chad:**
1. **Bear Tooth's diligence end:** the site had Nov 18, but his sheet says Nov 20. I kept Nov 18 because it may be a later correction. Whichever is right can be fixed on the lot's edit page.
2. **One line of his summary box is relabeled.** His "Lombardo owns and under contract to purchase" line only counted Lombardo and Pending lots, so it showed the same 6 lots and $2,044,900 as "Lombardo owns". I replaced it with the clearer split above; every dollar total is the same.
3. **107 Lock Dr** has no ownership or prices in his sheet, so it shows blank there.

The prices are visible to anyone with the site link until sign-in is built, which you said was fine for now. They aren't stored in the code on GitHub; I loaded them straight into the database.

I read "just for the zoning project" as meaning the Entire setup files, so I committed and pushed them in stl-zoning only. Your personal `settings.local.json` was left out. Entire is still switched on, uncommitted, in Parent-Hub, Veteran and W-Crew-app. If you meant Entire should only run on the zoning project, I can switch it off in those three.

**The test email to Chad did not go out, and the problem is bigger than this one email.** The sign-up saved, and I've deleted the test row since. But the email service the site uses (Resend) refused to send it with this message: "You can only send testing emails to your own email address (tbw0391@gmail.com). To send emails to other recipients, please verify a domain."

That same rule has blocked every email the site has tried to send since Oct 15: 176 failed sends. They include the Monday digests on Oct 19 and Oct 26 and the alert emails, all addressed to you and Chad. Even your copies failed, because each send included Chad and Resend rejects the whole message. The only emails that ever went out were the two tests on Oct 12–13 that went to you alone.

**The fix is a one-time setup on your side:**
1. At resend.com/domains, add a domain you own, for example AGA Technologies' website domain.
2. Resend shows 3–4 DNS records. Add them wherever that domain is registered (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Squarespace, etc.); it takes about 10 minutes.
3. Tell me the sending address you want, such as `tracker@yourdomain.com`. I'll switch the site's emails to it and send Chad the test sign-up again.

Do you have a domain I should use? If not, a cheap one bought through Resend or Vercel works too.

Here's how I'd separate it. It's the "companies" step that was planned next, and the team list I just built already has the slot for it.

**How it would work:**
- **Every private record gets an owner company:** projects, OYL lots, tasks, notes, watches, alerts and suggestions. Everything that exists today is tagged **Lombardo**.
- **Chad is on the Lombardo team.** When he signs in he sees exactly what he sees today: Lombardo's logo, projects, OYL lots, Chad's tasks, dashboard, alerts and digest. Nothing of yours or anyone else's.
- **You'd be on AGA Technologies as the admin.** You can switch between companies to see Lombardo's view, Ohio test accounts or future customers. Chad can't.
- **Public meeting data stays shared:** meetings, agendas, rezonings, votes, municipalities and contacts are collected once and everyone sees them. What's private is what each company adds on top.
- **Each company gets its own settings:** which cities and states it follows, its logo or the Hawkeye name, its weekly email recipients, and which opt-in features are on. Lombardo keeps Missouri; an Ohio customer gets Ohio.

**What that changes for Chad:** nothing visible. He signs in with a code and his site looks the same. The difference is that your work, the Ohio testing and future customers stay out of his view, and Lombardo's data stays out of theirs.

**The work:**
1. Add the company column and tag everything as Lombardo.
2. Lock each private table to "your company only".
3. Give you a company switcher.
4. Move followed cities, the logo and digest recipients into per-company settings.

It's a solid day of changes. I'd do it right after sign-in is switched on, since it builds on the team list.

Is that what you meant by breaking it out: Chad sees only Lombardo, and you see everything? Or did you mean something else, like giving Chad his own separate site or his own copy of the OYL tracker?

# BoathouseOS

PWA for rowing clubs: roster, schedule, lineups, volunteer needs,
team store link, and messaging.

## Stack

- Next.js 15 (App Router) + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- Supabase (Postgres, Auth, RLS)
- PWA via `@ducanh2912/next-pwa`

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # fill in Supabase project URL + anon key
npm run dev
```

## Database

Schema lives in `supabase/migrations/`. Apply with the Supabase CLI or paste
into the SQL editor of your Supabase project:

```bash
supabase db push
```

## PWA

The manifest is at `public/manifest.json`, icons in `public/icons/`
(placeholders — swap for real club branding). The service worker is
generated at build time and disabled in development.

team store link, and messaging.

## Stack

- Next.js 15 (App Router) + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- Supabase (Postgres, Auth, RLS)
- PWA via `@ducanh2912/next-pwa`

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # fill in Supabase project URL + anon key
npm run dev
```

## Database

Schema lives in `supabase/migrations/`. Apply with the Supabase CLI or paste
into the SQL editor of your Supabase project:

```bash
supabase db push
```

## PWA

The manifest is at `public/manifest.json`, icons in `public/icons/`
(placeholders — swap for real club branding). The service worker is
generated at build time and disabled in development.

content.text:
Yes, do separate tenants, the same way you split BoathouseOS. There, the public demo runs on its own Supabase database and its own Vercel deployment, apart from the real clubs. For Lombardo that's the strongest answer to an audit: their data sits in a database that holds nothing else. Even a leaked master key to Lombardo's database would expose only Lombardo, and a bug in our access rules can't leak another customer's data into their view.

**The conveniently easy part:** today's setup is already almost entirely Lombardo. So rather than moving Lombardo out, we move everything else out.

| | Lombardo's site (today's project, kept) | Public product, Project Hawkeye (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Database | Today's Supabase project: Lombardo's projects, OYL lots, tasks, and the Missouri meeting data | A new Supabase project: Ohio data, demo, sign-ups, future customers |
| Website | stl-zoning.vercel.app now, or a Lombardo address later | A new Vercel deployment, with its own address |
| Code | Same GitHub repo, with a setting that turns off the landing page, demo, sign-up and Ohio | Same repo, with the Lombardo-only pages switched off |
| Meeting collection | Its own daily collector for the Missouri cities | Its own collector for Ohio and new markets |

**What an auditor would find on Lombardo's side:**
- **Only Lombardo's data in the database.** No other customers, no sign-ups, no demo.
- **Sign-in required for everything,** limited to the team list, with codes rather than passwords. The open demo and sign-up page don't exist on their site.
- **"Behind their firewall" without them hosting it.** The site and database can be restricted to their office and VPN internet addresses through Vercel's firewall, so it's unreachable from outside their network. That usually satisfies the request.
- **They can own the accounts.** The Supabase and Vercel accounts for their site can belong to Lombardo, with AGA invited as the vendor. They can see every access and remove yours at any time. Auditors like that more than anything else on this list.
- **Things to finish either way:**
  - Make the GitHub repo private.
  - Turn on two-factor login on the GitHub, Supabase and Vercel accounts.
  - Turn off open sign-up.
  - Upgrade Supabase to Pro (about $25 a month per database) for daily backups, and for signing in with their company Microsoft account if they want that.
  - Write a one-page summary of security and data handling for their IT team.

**Order I'd do it in:**
1. Finish locking down today's project: sign-in required, data rules applied, open sign-up off, repo private. This is mostly done; it's waiting on your test sign-in.
2. Create the new Hawkeye Supabase and Vercel projects, move Ohio, the demo and sign-ups there, and delete them from Lombardo's database.
3. Add the per-site setting so one codebase builds both sites.
4. Optionally restrict Lombardo's site to their network and transfer account ownership to them.

The first step is the urgent one, and it's waiting on you: sign in once at /login so I can switch the requirement on. Steps 2–3 are about a day of work.

Want me to go ahead with that plan? I'd also need one decision: should the Supabase and Vercel accounts for Lombardo's site belong to **Lombardo** or stay under **AGA**? It changes how I set things up.

p='docs/HANDOFF.md'; s=open(p).read()
old='## Next up\n'
new='''## Next up
0. **Security and audit readiness (Oct 26; Lombardo asked about moving the tracker behind their firewall).** Goal: an audit of Lombardo's site can't reach anyone else's data. In order:
   a. Switch on sign-in: waiting on the user's first code sign-in at /login. Then apply supabase/pending/require_sign_in.sql (move it into migrations), set Vercel REQUIRE_SIGN_IN=1, redeploy, and check every page signed in and signed out.
   b. Supabase dashboard (user): turn off "Allow new users to sign up"; Twilio Verify as the phone provider (Account SID, Auth Token, Verify Service SID entered in the dashboard, never in chat); custom SMTP through Resend for auth emails (built-in email only reaches Supabase account members, so Chad can't get a code yet).
   c. Email is broken: Resend has no verified domain, so every digest, alert and sign-up notice to anyone but the user has failed since Oct 15 (digest_log). Verify a domain at resend.com/domains, then change DIGEST_FROM and resend the test sign-up to Chad.
   d. GitHub: make tbw0391/stl-zoning private (it was public on Oct 26; history scan found no keys), Dependabot alerts, protect main against force-push/deletion. Two-factor login on GitHub, Supabase, Vercel and the domain registrar.
   e. Separate tenants, like BoathouseOS's demo/production split: keep this Supabase + Vercel project as Lombardo's dedicated instance; create a new Supabase + Vercel project for Project Hawkeye (public product) and move Ohio jurisdictions/meetings, /welcome, /demo, /signup and signups there, then delete them here. One codebase, a per-deployment setting turning the public pages and Ohio off on Lombardo's site and the Lombardo pages off on Hawkeye's. Each runs its own collectors for its own cities.
   f. Lombardo options: restrict their site to their office/VPN IPs (Vercel firewall) as the "behind the firewall" answer; Supabase Pro for daily backups (and Microsoft SSO if wanted); decide whether Lombardo or AGA owns their Supabase/Vercel accounts (undecided); a one-page security summary for their IT.
   g. Within Hawkeye: companies (company column on private tables, RLS by company, admin switcher), building on team_members.company.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

I added the security and separate-tenant work to the to-do list in the developer notes (`docs/HANDOFF.md`), as item 0 at the top of "Next up". I left it off the Suggestions page because Chad's team reads that page. It covers seven steps:
- switching sign-in on
- the Supabase settings only you can change
- fixing email
- locking down GitHub
- splitting Lombardo onto its own site
- Lombardo's options (office-only access, backups, who owns the accounts)
- separating customers within the public product

The developer notes are in the GitHub repo, which is still public, so these plans are readable there until you make it private. That's one more reason to do that soon.

**Today's suggestions (#33–40):**

| # | Page | What they asked | My take |
|---|---|---|---|
| 33 | Dardenne Prairie page | Wants to add an Excel file so you can get its data onto the site | Almost certainly the OYL Tracker, which is now done. I'd mark it done. |
| 34 | Calendar | Show past meeting dates, not just future ones | Small: add a "Past" option or let the list scroll back. |
| 35 | Dashboard | A card can only be dropped on "Drop here", so a card at the bottom of a column can't be moved to the top | A bug in drag and drop. Dropping onto any spot in a column should work. Small fix. |
| 36 | Project 16 | "I put a duplicate project in and would like to delete one" | My doing, explained below. Also, there's no way to delete a project on the site, which is worth adding. |
| 37 | Calendar | Pick one, some or all municipalities instead of one or all | Small to medium: a checklist filter that remembers the choice. |
| 38 | Features | Email or post on the site when minutes come out for a meeting that discussed one of the projects | Medium. The site already reads minutes and matches projects by case number, so this adds the notice. |
| 39 | Suggestions | When an agenda is posted in a city with an active project, email a group or post it on the site | Medium. Similar to #38, using the existing agenda reader. |
| 40 | Alerts | Mark alerts as seen one at a time | Small. |

**About #36:** Chad added "1400 Bopp Rd" by hand (project 12) two minutes before I loaded his spreadsheet, and my import made a second one (project 16) that holds the lot details and prices. I'd move the lot details onto his project 12, which has the full address, and delete 16.

**#38 and #39 depend on email working.** Every email to Chad has failed since Oct 15, so those notices would only show on the site until a domain is verified in Resend.

Want me to fix #36 that way and work through the small ones (#34, #35, #40, plus a Delete button for projects)? Each change visible to Chad would ship switched off, ready for him to turn on in New features.
